title: 2017 HMMT February Team Problem 2
statement: Does there exist a two-variable polynomial \(P(x, y)\) with real number coefficients such that \(P(x, y)\) is positive exactly when \(x\) and \(y\) are both positive?

solutions.text:
Answer: No
For any \(\epsilon\) and positive \(x, P(x, \epsilon)>0\) and \(P(x,-\epsilon) \leq 0\). Thus by continuity/IVT, \(P(x, 0)=0\) for all positive \(x\). Similarly \(P(0, y)=0\) for all positive \(y\). This implies \(x y \mid P(x, y)\), and so we can write \(P(x, y)=x y Q(x, y)\). But then this same logic holds for \(Q\), and this cannot continue infinitely unless \(P\) is identically 0 - in which case the conditions do not hold. So no such polynomial exists.
